mat.name: DHM (Dihydromyrcenol)
mat.note:
NOTE POSITION : Top to Top-Mid

FRAGRANCE FAMILY : Fresh Citrus, Aquatic/Marine, Fougère

FACETS : Fresh · Citrus-Lime · Marine · Clean · Terpenic

TENACITY : Medium-High — detectable on skin for 4 to 6 hours; significantly longer on fabric and paper

SILLAGE : High — strong diffusion and projection, particularly pronounced in the first 1 to 2 hours after application heat-stable.

mat.name: Hedione
mat.note: BioShop: EDP 3–15%, not IFRA restricted. Adds air rather than smell — florals sit flat without it. AVOID pairing with strong phenolics like eugenol at high dose; the sharpness competes with its transparency.
mat.pairs: Iso E Super; Galaxolide; Rose Oxide; Linalool; Bergamot

mat.name: Galaxolide
mat.note: BioShop pairings: +Iso E Super = Grojsman/Eternity base · +PEA = rose musk · +Coumarin = fougere musk · +Geraniol 3–5% = rose-geranium lift. Musk anosmia is common — blend structurally different musks (Ethylene Brassylate, Cashmeran) rather than relying on this alone.

mat.name: Ethylene Brassylate
mat.note: Soft clean macrocyclic musk. BioShop: 1–10% of concentrate, 2–6% typical. Reads banana to me specifically — check with a fresh nose before correcting for it.

mat.name: Iso E Super
mat.note: The Grojsman base: Iso E 10% + Galaxolide 8% is the structural foundation of most modern masculine formulas. Smooths and diffuses. Above 30% it stops supporting and becomes the effect itself.

mat.name: Coumarin
mat.note: Toasted hay-almond, the fougere backbone. BioShop: bridges vanillin sweetness to dry amber resins. Lasts 400+ hours on a strip — strong fixative. IFRA 1.5% of finished perfume (corrected from 3.0%). A 10% stock is a trace tool — pure powder needed for a coumarin-forward fougere.

acc.name: Musk-amber base
acc.note: Batch 002. From 10% dilutions at 3:3:1. All base notes — stable enough to judge in one sitting.

acc.name: Citrus opening
acc.note: Batch 003. Citral pulled back from the original proportion. Fades while you evaluate — note the time at each observation.

form.name: First Rain
form.note: Fresh, airy, built for heat. Citrus over clean musk.

form.name: Climate
form.note: Rebuilt — Bergamot removed. It exceeded the 0.4% IFRA phototoxicity limit at 1.08% of finished product (2.7x over), and was already the weaker heat-stability choice vs Petitgrain. Its 6% redistributed to Petitgrain (+4) and DHM (+2). Dry transparent base still carries the identity — judge at day 14, not day 3.

form.name: Citrus Root
form.note: Cologne structure — bright top, earthy base, no heart. Built to isolate Iso E Super from Vetiver in the drydown.

form.name: Slow Amber
form.note: Restrained gourmand. Linalool cut 18% -> 5% — at the old level it dominated the top and its camphoraceous facet read as medicinal. Benzoin also cut 18% -> 13% to clear the 2% IFRA ceiling (was 2.70%, now 1.95%). Freed percentage went to Hedione, Sandenol, Galaxolide and Ambroxan. Note the top is now genuinely thin — that is the gap Slow Amber II fills.

form.name: Rose Study
form.note: PEA-led. Won't read as full rose — four of its five pillars are missing. Note what feels absent.

form.name: Inverted gourmand base
form.note: Woody oriental base for the three-variant restraint exercise — add Benzoin at 5% (A) / 12% (B) / 25% (C), scaling this base down to match, to find where a gourmand facet stops being a signal and becomes the subject.
form.parked: Needs Coumarin + lactones from T2 to test against a real gourmand accord — Benzoin alone would mostly repeat Slow Amber.

form.name: Driftwood
form.note: Beach, sea air, solitude — the arc built into the structure: a brief citrus opening giving way to Vetiver and Ambroxan settling into Iso E Super's quiet base. Citral reduced from 9% to 3.5% (was 2.25x over the IFRA limit); DHM added at 5.5% to carry the "brief pulse" role instead, using the established DHM+Citral pairing logic.
form.parked: Needs Cypriol for genuine heart-position smoke. This version is IFRA-compliant and buildable now, but doesn't yet deliver the smoke thesis Driftwood was designed around.

form.name: Slow Amber II
form.note: Slow Amber II — three-accord structure. TOP: Sweet Orange leads (cardamom dropped on cost; orange bridges into caramel better than a green spice would). CARAMEL HEART: ethyl maltol at 1.5% does the work, coumarin adds toasted depth, vanillin rounds, PEA honeys, nonalactone creams; Hedione carries the lift jasmine would have. AMBER BASE: Benzoin capped at 13% for the 2% IFRA ceiling, 3% Vetiver as dry contrast — without it the added caramel rebuilds the cloying problem.
form.parked: Needs Ethyl Maltol, Vanillin, Cinnamyl Alcohol, Coumarin and gamma-Nonalactone from T2.

bat.note:
Labdanum replaced by pushing linalool to 0.28 from 0.13g.
Result is a synthetic citrus heavy opening,  but a clean resiny mid and drydown. Almost caramel like.

evals.n: Overpowering linalool, 10 mins - linalool fading and resin emerging, 30 mins - linalool gone but still present for a fresh nose.
Linalool not so overpowering but still there, 10 mins - same plus resin, maybe bring linalool down to increase toffee aspect more.

notes.text: Ambroxan is pre-diluted 10% in IPM. Supplier guidance is 0.5–4% of the finished formula — weigh it directly, no conversion.
IPM and ethanol lose miscibility above roughly 22–27% IPM by weight. Keep IPM-carried materials to a small share of any ethanol blend.
Serial dilution — a 10% stock diluted 10× again — is the correct route to 1%. Don't weigh tiny neat quantities.
Vessel cleaning after oily or musk-heavy batches: ethanol → warm water with unscented soap → ethanol → air-dry inverted → sniff-test before reuse.
Musks are tenacious. Consider dedicated glassware for that family.

Personal calibration: Ethylene Brassylate reads as banana to me — a macrocyclic musk facet others may not perceive. Confirmed directly (Galaxolide alone does not carry it). Check with a fresh nose before correcting a formula for it.
Olfactory adaptation is real. My own reading on a blend I've been living with is unreliable. Hand the strip to someone fresh.
Maceration is driven by naturals and resinoids present, not by "heaviness". All-synthetic → 1 week. Naturals → 2. Resinoids → 3+.
Blotter ≠ skin. A blotter says what a blend IS; skin says what it DOES.

Distinguishing two quiet materials (e.g. Hedione vs Ethylene Brassylate): test at 24hr for tenacity, or raise concentration to ~20–25% temporarily rather than going lower — both are too faint at 1% to grip.
Check every material's actual sold form (neat vs pre-diluted) before assuming. Confirmed true for Ambroxan; worth a single pass to confirm the rest.
IFRA limits in this app are Category 4 (fine fragrance), percent of finished product, seeded from memory — unverified until checked against the real Standard and marked so.

Ethyl maltol is the caramel molecule and the most dangerous thing in the kit for cloying. 0.5-2% of concentrate, never more. When adding sweetness, add dryness alongside it (vetiver, dry woods) or you rebuild the exact Janaan Vanilla failure.
